words.meaning: to gather separate things into a cluster or compact mass
words.example: Small delays can agglomerate into a serious backlog by the end of the quarter.

words.meaning: a practical shortcut or rule of thumb used to make decisions or solve problems
words.example: As a quick heuristic, we prioritize requests that affect the most customers.

words.meaning: explaining something in terms of its purpose or intended result
words.example: Her teleological argument judged every process by whether it improved the customer experience.

words.meaning: charging an unfairly or excessively high rate of interest
words.example: The owner rejected the loan because its usurious terms would strain the business.

words.meaning: the return of something unpleasant after a period of improvement or inactivity
words.example: A recrudescence of payment fraud prompted the company to tighten its controls.

phrases.term: make a federal case out of it
phrases.meaning: to treat a minor issue as if it were extremely serious
phrases.example: I forgot to attach one file, but there is no need to make a federal case out of it.

phrases.term: have a dog in the fight
phrases.meaning: to have a personal interest in the outcome of a dispute or competition
phrases.example: I do not have a dog in the fight, so I can evaluate both proposals fairly.

phrases.meaning: to deceive or trick someone successfully
phrases.example: The seller tried to put one over on us by hiding the car's repair history.

phrases.meaning: to take a chance on something uncertain or risky
phrases.example: We decided to take a flier on the small startup because its prototype looked promising.

phrases.meaning: to develop a sudden, unusual urge to do something
phrases.example: He got a wild hair and repainted the kitchen over the weekend.
